summary: Feed s173_triple is degraded: 25.4% duplicates, 100% missing VLAN 10/20 tags, and 1.3% TCP gaps impair IDS detection coverage.

findings.root_cause: Aggregation without deduplication - same packets forwarded twice via overlapping SPAN/mirror sessions (ingress+egress or dual uplinks) through packet broker with no dedup window.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS wastes ~25% of its 1G capacity on duplicates, inflates state tables, skews thresholds and risks missing real attacks due to processing overhead and duplicate alerts.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet-broker deduplication to suppress identical packets within a short window before delivery to IDS, restoring capacity and accurate detection.

findings.root_cause: 802.1Q tags stripped at source or broker - 100% packets untagged despite IDS requiring VLANs 10 and 20, indicating SPAN from access ports or broker policy stripping VLAN headers.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS cannot apply VLAN-aware policies or segment traffic for VLANs 10/20; loses tenant/zone context causing blind spots and misattribution.

recommended_fix.why: Configure source trunk/SPAN to preserve 802.1Q and set broker to forward tags intact so IDS receives required VLAN 10/20 context.

findings.root_cause: Lossy SPAN/mirror or broker buffer drops - 55 of 4349 TCP packets (1.3% >1% threshold) show gaps/retransmissions while tool_overload is healthy, pointing to source oversubscription not IDS overload.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS TCP reassembly and stream signature matching fail on gapped flows; allows evasion and missed payload inspection.

recommended_fix.why: Replace lossy SPAN with physical TAP and ensure broker buffering/bandwidth is sufficient for lossless delivery to IDS.
